long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan was born in Abu Dhabi, studied political science at UAE University and entered federal service through the Ministry of Information and Culture. He later led that ministry before becoming foreign minister in 2006. A son of UAE founder Sheikh Zayed, his standing follows the Al Nahyan dynasty and public office; reliable sources do not identify a separate wealth-producing business or distinguish a personal fortune from wider family holdings.

As foreign minister, Abdullah became a central figure in the UAE's external relations and signed the Abraham Accords on the country's behalf in 2020. He added the deputy premiership in 2024 while retaining the foreign-affairs portfolio. His official biography also describes him as an avid reader of history and keen scuba diver. Abu Dhabi's sovereign investment assets are not treated as his property: ADIA states that it invests funds supplied by, and returned to, the Government of Abu Dhabi.
